title: Silver Lime: Ancient Silver Limes You Can Visit
meta_description: A lime whose leaves flicker silver in the wind, mapped in a castle park, a former private garden and a Dutch town that may take its own name from the tree.
intro: Silver lime carries its identifying trick on the underside of every leaf: a coat of fine white felt that flickers the whole crown between green and silver on a windy day, readable from thirty metres away. Four trees are mapped here, and no two arrived the same way. Tilburg's oldest tree, standing off the main square where nobody thinks to look, grows in a town that may take its own name from the species. A second Tilburg lime, in a small park on the Fokkerpad, once stood in a private garden laid out by the landscape architect Leonard Springer before the estate opened to the public. Helmond's was planted just after Kasteel Helmond changed hands in 1921, the last tree of the old private park rather than a survivor of it. Amersfoort's is grafted, a weeping 'Petiolaris' crown joined onto an ordinary lime rootstock, two plants sharing one trunk, its long leaf stalks letting each leaf swivel independently in the wind.
